audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Ignition (W) does not appear once in either layer, and the itemization line actively dismisses the counter to it: 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal'. Silver Stake (P) is also never named, so the page attributes all of the low-HP danger to Purgatory alone.
audit.why: Soul Ignition costs Locke current health per second, then heals a portion of that damage back at the end of the duration — 18s at rank 1. Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of where it comes from, so it cuts that refund and leaves him having simply paid the health. Describing the refund as 'not lifesteal' is true and irrelevant; the conclusion drawn from it is wrong. Silver Stake is on-hit magic damage that grows with the target's missing health, which is the real reason 'never linger at low HP' is correct — his autos are already scaling up before the ult is ever thrown.
audit.corrected: Name Soul Ignition and its 18s heal-back as a Grievous Wounds target, and attribute the low-HP danger to Silver Stake as well as Purgatory.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers score all seven rows Cho'Gath. The packet chart says Skill at Levels 1, 2, 3 and 6, and the content layer's own whys say exactly that: 'Level 1 is even', 'Level 2 stays even skill', 'Level 3 is still skill-based poke trading', 'Level 6 is even in the immediate window'.
audit.why: 52.61% over 555 games is a mildly favoured lane, not a seven-row sweep. The whys array contradicts the win array it sits next to, row for row, on four of seven rows.
audit.corrected: Chart becomes Skill, Skill, Skill, Cho'Gath, Skill, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath with ratings 5, 5, 5, 7, 5, 6, 7.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. That is true of the content layer — early, mid and late contain no numbers at all — even though the full layer already has good sequencing.
audit.why: Ritual Nails is 10s at rank 1 and 950 range, exactly matching Rupture's reach, so the range war is genuinely even and the window is the seconds after he throws. Ashen Pursuit is 10s flat at every rank and is his only mobility, so a spent blink is a fixed ten-second window you can count. Purgatory is 120s at rank 1 and 1000 range.
audit.corrected: Put the 10s Ritual Nails, 10s-flat Ashen Pursuit and 120s Purgatory numbers into the content early/mid paragraphs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two of the three Critical Don'ts carry descriptions belonging to a different heading. 'Fight at sliver HP inside Purgatory' is explained with text about his E being engage and escape; 'Let him free-shove and roam' is explained with the trade-bad line about nail marks.
audit.why: The headings are correct and useful; the bodies point the reader at the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Rewrite both descriptions to match their headings, using Silver Stake and Purgatory's 1000 range respectively.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Grievous Wounds still cuts Soul Ignition's 18s heal-back — a refund is healing.

edits.before: E is his engage AND escape — a spent blink is the lane’s biggest cooldown; don’t waste yours before it.
edits.after: Silver Stake grows with your missing health, so the lower you are the harder his autos already hit.

edits.before: Fighting with 2-3 nail marks on you while his E is up — that’s his entire kill script, pre-paid.
edits.after: A shoved-in Locke roams to execute chipped lanes, and Purgatory reaches 1000 units to do it.

edits.before: Locke wastes Ritual Nails — that is your full-commit window.
edits.after: Purgatory is 120s at rank 1 — outside it, you are simply bigger.

edits.before: An honest poke war through level 3: your Q knockup and Vorpal Spikes trade evenly with his Q poke and on-hit chip, so contest calmly and don't bleed HP for nothing. From 4-5 the lane starts leaning your way — you're approaching 6 and the Feast HP curve he cannot match. Just reach your ult healthy.
edits.after: An honest poke war through level 3: Ritual Nails is 10s at rank 1 and reaches 950, the same as Rupture, so step up in the seconds after he throws it. Ashen Pursuit is 10s flat and it is his only exit — a spent blink is your Rupture window. From 4-5 the lane leans your way. Reach 6 healthy.

edits.before: Level 6 is the last stage where his ult math genuinely threatens you, so respect his R until your first Feast stacks land. From there, every stack plus your first HP item shoves your health pool past Purgatory's execute threshold and his kill condition quietly dies. Silence his trade patterns with W and start bullying.
edits.after: Level 6 is the last stage where his ult math genuinely threatens you, so respect Purgatory's 120s until your first Feast stacks land. From there, every stack plus your first HP item shoves your pool past its execute threshold and his kill condition quietly dies. Grievous Wounds cuts Soul Ignition's heal-back — then start bullying.

edits.before: Full Feast bulk ends the conversation — his execute totem simply cannot reach your health pool, and true damage plus knockups let you run him over on repeat. Frontline every fight, Feast whatever he tries to protect, and remember: he needs a miracle window; you just need to walk at him.
edits.after: Full Feast bulk ends the conversation — his execute totem cannot reach your health pool, and Feast's true damage plus knockups run him over on repeat. Silver Stake still scales off your missing health, so top up before you re-engage. He needs a miracle window; you just walk at him.

edits.before: The even poke war peaks — your Q knockup and Vorpal Spikes against his chip, with neither side able to force a kill.
edits.after: The even poke war peaks — Ritual Nails is 10s at rank 1 and 950 range, the same reach as Rupture, so neither forces a kill.

notes: UNVERIFIED, left alone: the full layer says twice that Locke is 'a 125-range mana champ'. His attack range is not in champ-data/_kits/locke.json and 125 is short even for a melee champion, so I could not confirm or refute it and did not touch either sentence. Same for the '~15%' execute floor in phases[4].why — Riot's text says only 'potentially executes'. FLAG MISFIRE, not written: the kit tags Purgatory with 'grounding'; Riot's description says only that it binds, damages and potentially executes. It is moot for Cho'Gath, who has no dash, so I made no claim. Level chart: four rows flip to Skill in both layers as one atomic group, matching the packet and the content whys.
